1: # AI Agent Instructions (AGENTS.md)
2: 
3: Factory app repo: the process contract lives in
4: [factory-kit](https://github.com/awingrove/factory-kit) — this file holds
5: the stack rules and directives specific to this repo. If this file and the
6: kit disagree, that is a defect: report it, don't pick a side.
7: 
8: **Response style:** smart caveman — cut filler, keep technical substance.
9: Fragments fine. Technical terms stay exact; code blocks unchanged.
10: 
11: ## Stack rules (static JS)
12: 
13: - **Zero runtime dependencies.** Browser code is vanilla ESM
14:   (`<script type="module">`); devDeps only (eslint, prettier, vitest,
15:   @playwright/test, yaml). No framework, no bundler, no build step.
16: - **No inline handlers, inline scripts, or inline styles.** The static
17:   server sends `script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'` — an inline-script
18:   temptation is a defect to report, not a CSP to relax. Wire behavior with
19:   `addEventListener` in external JS.
20: - **External JS lives under `js/` only**, one directory per slice
21:   (`js/sim/**`, `js/panel/**`); CSS under `css/` per slice. Pages reference
22:   them with relative paths.
23: - **Serving:** `node scripts/static-server.mjs --port <port>` (Playwright's
24:   `webServer` runs it for e2e). A manual peek may use any static server;
25:   the gate is always the node script — it carries the CSP headers.
26: - **File size:** production modules (`js/**`, `css/**`) over **300 lines**,
27:   test suites (`test/**`, `e2e/**`) over **450 lines**, or static HTML pages
28:   (`*.html`) over **550 lines** fail `scripts/guard-file-size.mjs`. Split by
29:   responsibility — in JS that means new modules, not partials.
30: - **Determinism:** `js/sim/**` never calls `Math.random()` or `Date.now()`.
31:   Seeded RNG only (`js/sim/rng.js`); time advances by explicit tick. This
32:   is what makes overload teachable and e2e assertions stable.
33: 
34: ## Modeling rules (executable conceptual model)
35: 
36: - **Executable conceptual model, not a statistical simulator.** Each stack
37:   component (`Browser`, `Network`, `WebServer`, and later `DNS`,
38:   `LoadBalancer`, `Cache`, `Database`, `WorkerQueue`, `Router`/`Bridge`)
39:   must be a small, directly readable JS implementation of its real
40:   responsibility, exchanging recognisable messages through the tick loop.
41:   Never fake a component's mechanism with probabilities (e.g. a cache hit
42:   must be an actual `Map` lookup on the request path with tick-based TTL,
43:   never `rng() < hitRate`). Trace and UI narratives are part of that
44:   contract: hop text and frames must consume the components' actual
45:   messages (the served record, queue state), not a hardcoded story
46:   (DL-1, DL-3, DL-4).
47: - **Slimmed-down protocols.** Every token on the wire must earn its
48:   teaching place. HTTP requests are `"GET /path"` (no `HTTP/1.1` or `\r\n`
49:   header boilerplate unless a stage specifically teaches headers);
50:   responses are `"<status> <body>"` (e.g. `"200 Welcome to the home page"`,
51:   `"404 Page not found"`).
52: - **Two-number mini-IP addresses (`<net>.<host>`).** Network addresses use
53:   two numbers — network and interface (e.g. `10.1`, `10.2`, `20.1`) —
54:   instead of 4-octet dotted quads. Stage 1 starts IP-only (`Browser` sends
55:   to `10.1` over `Network`); `DNS` (`example.com` → `10.x`) and cross-network
56:   routing/bridges (`10.x` ↔ `20.x`) enter only in the stages where they
57:   earn their teaching place.
58: 
59: ## AI workflow directives
60: 
61: 1. **Understand context** before modifying a file: pages → `js/panel` →
62:    `js/sim`; a change ripples outward, not downward.
63: 2. **Resumable boundary briefs (≤ 120 lines) & sub-agent execution:** work
64:    beyond ~3 tasks gets a committed brief at `docs/plans/<feature>.md` with
65:    checkbox steps; a tick means the step's commit exists (kit PLAN-FORMAT).
66:    - **No ghost-coding in briefs:** keep briefs **≤ 120 lines** (enforced by
67:      `scripts/guard-plan-ticks.mjs`). The lead session reads only the files
68:      needed to frame the design gate and specifies **boundary contracts only**
69:      (module exports, option/snapshot shapes, ring/node IDs, DOM
70:      `data-testid`s, and test titles) — never line-by-line helper code.
71:    - **Negative-case contracts (DL-3/DL-4):** any boundary contract whose
72:      behavior conditions on input — trace narratives, component responses,
73:      lane geometry, routing — must state the mechanism's branch conditions
74:      with one named counter-example ("a GET trace keeps the Stage 4 story;
75:      no async 202"), and §Tests must pin it. A contract written only as the
76:      happy-path script is a Step-1 defect: the executor cannot read intent
77:      the brief does not encode.
78:    - **3-step brief lifecycle:**
79:      - **Step 1 (Lead session):** after human design sign-off, commit
80:        `DESIGN.md` + `docs/plans/<feature>.md` (with Step 1 ticked `- [x]`,
81:        Steps 2–3 unticked `- [ ]`).
82:      - **Step 2 (`executor` sub-agent):** dispatch `subagent` with
83:        `agent: "executor"` on the model pinned in `.opencode/agents/executor.md`
84:        (executing on any other model is a process deviation to record) to
85:        implement the code, tests, and `slices.yaml` / `storymap.yaml` updates
86:        cold from the brief, tick `- [x] Step 2`, and commit with
87:        `npm run verify` green.
88:      - **Step 3 (Lead session):** run
89:        `npm run metrics:extract -- <subagentSessionID>`, append the entry
90:        (including true in-session `guardrail_failures`) to
91:        `docs/factory/slice-metrics.yaml`, tick `- [x] Step 3` in the brief,
92:        and commit with `npm run verify` green. The lead review also checks
93:        brief-contract tests exist (brief §Tests, including the negative-case
94:        pins) and that storymap/slices test refs pin the story's own behavior —
95:        a story marked done whose refs name stale or unrelated tests is a
96:        defect (DL-3). **Acceptance probe:** before opening the PR, the lead
97:        demos the slice end to end from the brief's contracts — scripted e2e
98:        counts — walking each boundary contract including its named counter-
99:        example; the probe reopens Step 2 on failure. Human screenshot rounds
100:        found DL-1 and DL-3 because this probe did not exist (DL-2 rule: what
101:        you do not demo, the human discovers).
102: 3. **Debug hygiene:** temporary probes are tracked as todos and removed
103:    before commit — never ride along in a feature diff.
104: 4. **Post-mortem, human-intervention & metrics capture:** a fix — or an
105:    unprompted human intervention correcting a code or process miss outside
106:    scheduled human gates — whose root cause reveals a systemic gap updates
107:    `docs/factory/technical-debt.yaml` (`DL-\d+`) and the rule doc in the same
108:    change (kit DEBT-REGISTER). Every completed brief records its intervention
109:    counts and sub-agent session telemetry (`opencode session export <id>`) in
110:    `docs/factory/slice-metrics.yaml` (kit METRICS).
111: 5. **Claim vocabulary:** guarantee-comments carry `CHECKS:` / `PINS:` /
112:    `DOCUMENTS:` — guarantee-language outside a claim is a review defect
113:    (kit CLAIM-LANGUAGE). A `PINS:` claim must name a real, resolvable pin
114:    (`test file::title` that exists) or be omitted — an aspirational pin is
115:    a defect (TD-6).
116: 6. **Manifests same-change:** `slices.yaml` + `storymap.yaml` change in the
117:    same commit as the feature they describe; a stale map is a defect
118:    (kit SLICES).
119: 7. **Design:** UI that introduces or alters a visual pattern raises the
120:    `DESIGN.md` amendment question with the human and updates `DESIGN.md` in
121:    the same change (kit DESIGN + DESIGN-REVIEW patterns).
122: 8. **Periodic full review:** when the cadence triggers — 8 delivered
123:    entries in `docs/factory/slice-metrics.yaml` since the last full
124:    review, or the first slice-merge of a month, whichever comes first —
125:    the lead session _prompts the human_ to run (or defer) a deep review
126:    per [factory-kit FULL-REVIEW.md](https://github.com/awingrove/factory-kit/blob/main/FULL-REVIEW.md):
127:    chunk map → fact briefs → verified per-chunk reviews → ranked
128:    assessment, findings registered as TD rows and staged as brief-sized
129:    fixes. Instruments are evidence named in the map, never gates; a
130:    targeted 1–3-chunk review does not reset the cadence. The prompt
131:    never fires on its own.
132: 
133: ## Gates
134: 
135: - `npm run verify` = format:check → lint → unit → guard → e2e. It is the
136:   **named** gate; never reimplement it ad hoc at the call site.
137: - **Red gate = stop**, fix the named cause. Second rejection of the same
138:   gate = stop and report to the human. Never weaken a guardrail, test, or
139:   manifest entry to pass (kit FACTORY gate-rejection rule).
140: 
141: ## GitHub identity
142: 
143: Shells authenticate as `awingrove-opencode` via
144: `.opencode/plugins/agent-identity.js` (token file + isolated `GH_CONFIG_DIR`,
145: fail-closed sentinel). Runbook:
146: [factory-kit AGENT-IDENTITY.md](https://github.com/awingrove/factory-kit/blob/main/AGENT-IDENTITY.md).
147: Agents push feature branches and open PRs — never approve, merge, delete,
148: or force-push (server-side rulesets, human-only bypass). Closing the agent's
149: own PRs is permitted.
150: 
151: ## PR handling (user-directed, 2026-10-26)
152: 
153: - **Reviewer assignment:** every PR the agent opens requests `awingrove` as
154:   a reviewer at creation time. The agent token has `repo` scope only, so
155:   `gh pr edit --add-reviewer` fails on GraphQL `read:org`; use the REST call
156:   instead (this is how PR #21's review was requested):
157:   `gh api repos/awingrove/stack-orrery/pulls/<n>/requested_reviewers -X POST -f 'reviewers[]=awingrove'`
158: - **PR notes:** every PR the agent opens follows the kit's PR-body shape
159:   ([factory-kit PR-NOTES.md](https://github.com/awingrove/factory-kit/blob/main/PR-NOTES.md)):
160:   decision half on top (TL;DR, ranked review path with time cost,
161:   explicit decisions-needed, ≤3-area risk map, named-gate verification),
162:   full audit trail collapsed in a record block; finding/register ids get
163:   one-line plain-English anchors, never prose-only.
164: - **Fixes ride open PRs:** while one of our PRs is still open, fixes to code
165:   in its scope land on its branch in a follow-up commit (full `npm run verify`
166:   green before the commit, same as any commit), not as a separate PR. A
167:   separate PR is warranted only when the fix is unrelated to the open PR's
168:   content.
